title: Thai Herb Marinated Tofu and Mushroom Skewers
summary: This vibrant plant-based dish features fragrant lemongrass, fresh galangal, and crushed kaffir lime leaves infused into extra firm tofu and meaty king oyster mushroom cubes. Prepared using traditional mortar-and-pestle aromatic pastes, the ingredients soak up layers of spicy, sweet, and tangy flavors before being threaded onto wooden skewers. A rich coconut cream basting sauce enhances the moisture, ensuring every piece acquires a slight caramelized edge over hot hardwood charcoal. Served alongside a quick cucumber chili relish and toasted peanuts, this recipe highlights how plant-centered regional cooking can deliver full-bodied depth without meat. The dish is ideal for outdoor gatherings or indoor grill pans, providing a high-protein option packed with colorful vegetables, crisp herbs, and aromatic seasonings. Every component works in harmony to balance the classic four pillars of Southeast Asian cuisine: salty, sour, sweet, and fiery heat. Enjoy these hot skewers as a primary course paired with steamed jasmine rice or warm sticky rice for a complete, satisfying dinner experience.

steps.step: Trim the tough outer stalks of the fresh lemongrass and slice the inner bulbs thinly.
Peel the fresh galangal root carefully using a spoon and slice it into small rounds.
Peel the garlic cloves and shallots, then chop them coarsely into uniform pieces.
Clean the coriander roots thoroughly under cold water to remove all traces of soil.
Place the sliced lemongrass and galangal into a heavy granite mortar and pestle.
Pound the fibrous root pieces firmly until they break down into coarse fibers.
Add the prepared garlic cloves, shallots, and coriander roots to the mortar mixture.
Pound continuously in a circular motion until a thick, uniform paste forms.
Measure out the ground white pepper, ground cumin, coriander seeds, and turmeric powder.
Add the dry ground spices directly into the mortar with the pounded aromatic roots.
Finely slice the red thai chilies and incorporate them into the paste for mild heat.
Pound for another three minutes until the spice oils release and color turns yellow.
Pour in two tablespoons of soy sauce to moisten the spice paste inside the mortar.
Add one tablespoon of thin dark soy sauce to deepen the color and savory flavor base.
Spoon in the coconut sugar and pound gently to dissolve the crystals completely.
Drizzle in one tablespoon of melted coconut oil while stirring the paste thoroughly.
Tear the fresh kaffir lime leaves into small bits, discarding the tough central veins.
Add the torn lime leaf bits into the mortar and crush them to release citrus oils.
Taste the paste mixture carefully and adjust with a small pinch of sea salt if needed.
Scrape the finished aromatic paste out into a wide glass bowl using a rubber spatula.
Set the bowl of aromatic paste aside at room temperature while preparing the protein.
Unwrap the block of firm tofu and drain the excess packing liquid into the sink.
Wrap the tofu block tightly in layers of clean paper towels to absorb moisture.
Place a flat cutting board on top of the wrapped tofu and weigh it down for fifteen minutes.
Unwrap the pressed tofu and slice it carefully into two-centimeter square cubes.
Wipe the king oyster mushrooms clean with a damp paper towel to remove any dirt.
Trim off the stem ends of the mushrooms and cut the trunks into matching thick rounds.
Deseed the red bell pepper and cut the flesh into square chunks equal to the tofu.
Peel the red onion and cut it into wedges, separating the layers into wide petals.
Transfer the tofu cubes gently into the wide bowl containing the prepared aromatic paste.
Add the mushroom rounds, pepper squares, and onion petals into the bowl as well.
Toss the ingredients gently using rubber tongs to coat every piece evenly with paste.
Pour fifty milliliters of coconut milk over the ingredients to help marinade stick.
Cover the glass marinade bowl tightly with plastic wrap to trap the fresh aromas.
Place the bowl into the refrigerator and let the ingredients marinate for thirty minutes.
Submerge twelve wooden bamboo skewers in a shallow pan filled with warm tap water.
Soak the skewers for twenty minutes to prevent them from scorching during grilling.
Combine diced cucumber, thin chilies, and scallions in a small bowl for the relish.
Whisk rice vinegar, water, sugar, and salt together until clear to make the dressing.
Pour the sweet vinegar mixture over the cucumber relish and stir gently to combine.
Remove the marinated tofu and vegetable mixture from the refrigerator after thirty minutes.
Remove the bamboo skewers from the water bath and shake off excess surface moisture.
Pour remaining coconut milk into a small saucepan over medium heat for the baste glaze.
Add tamarind paste, sweet chili sauce, and palm sugar into the warming coconut milk.
Stir the glaze constantly until the palm sugar completely melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Remove the glaze pan from heat and whisk in one teaspoon of toasted sesame oil.
Thread one piece of marinated red bell pepper onto the pointed end of a soaked skewer.
Follow with a cube of marinated firm tofu, pushing it down gently to join the pepper.
Add a petal of red onion onto the skewer next, securing it flat against the tofu cube.
Thread a piece of king oyster mushroom onto the skewer, keeping spacing tight and neat.
Repeat the pattern with another piece of pepper, tofu, onion, and mushroom on the skewer.
Finish the skewer with a final red pepper square to lock all ingredients in place.
Lay the assembled skewer onto a parchment-lined baking sheet and repeat for remaining items.
Ensure each skewer leaves two inches of bare handle at the bottom for easy turning.
Spoon remaining marinade from the bowl over the threaded skewers for maximum flavor.
Mix peanut butter, hot water, and lime juice in a cup to form a smooth dip side sauce.
Set the small bowl of peanut dip sauce next to the cucumber relish on the serving tray.
Preheat your indoor cast iron grill pan or outdoor charcoal grill to high heat.
Lightly oil the grill grates using a folded paper towel dipped in neutral coconut oil.
Arrange the prepared skewers onto the hot grill pan in a single layer with space between.
Brush the top side of each skewer generously with the warm coconut tamarind glaze.
Listen for a steady sizzle, indicating the grill heat is high enough for crisp sear marks.
Keep the remaining glaze nearby with a pastry brush for frequent basting during cook.
Grill the skewers undisturbed for three minutes until deep char marks form on the bottom.
Use metal tongs to carefully turn each skewer ninety degrees onto its adjacent side.
Brush the freshly turned top surface with another layer of warm coconut tamarind glaze.
Allow the second side to grill for two to three minutes until caramelized and tender.
Turn each skewer again to expose the third side to the direct heat of the grill pan.
Apply more coconut glaze evenly over the tofu and mushrooms while they continue cooking.
Monitor heat closely to ensure sweet glaze caramelizes without burning black on grates.
Rotate skewers to the final side and cook for two minutes until thoroughly heated.
Check that mushroom pieces are tender and edges of tofu cubes are pleasantly crisp.
Brush a final thin layer of glaze over all sides of the hot skewers right on grill.
Transfer hot skewers from the grill pan onto a clean warm wooden serving platter.
Sprinkle crushed roasted peanuts generously over the entire length of the skewers.
Garnish the platter with fresh cilantro leaves, fresh thai basil, and chopped mint.
Scatter white sesame seeds over the top for added visual appeal and subtle nutty crunch.
Scatter finely chopped scallions across the skewers for a fresh green color pop.
Place fresh lime wedges along the edge of the platter for optional table squeezing.
Set the cucumber chili relish bowl on the platter next to the warm tofu skewers.
Place the small dish of smooth peanut dipping sauce beside the cucumber relish bowl.
Verify that all skewers are arranged neatly with handles facing outward for guests.
Serve immediately while skewers are piping hot and aromatics are intensely fragrant.
Pair with bowls of hot steamed jasmine rice or traditional sticky rice for dinner.
